about.changelog.directorConfirm: The same confirmation card is no longer asked twice: answer it in the task and the Work Director's copy closes as handled.
about.changelog.employees: Employees created by the Work Director are folded into one group in the task list, with the count and what is running on its header, so your own tasks are not pushed off screen.
about.changelog.line1: Context compression in task workspaces now really shrinks the context, and compressing again no longer rewrites the old summary.
about.changelog.line2: Long conversations and tasks no longer get slower the longer they run; typing and scrolling stay responsive while an answer streams.
about.changelog.line3: A workspace whose folder was deleted or whose SSH host is unreachable is now marked in the list.
about.changelog.line4: Closing the window can minimize to tray or quit; double-click the tray icon to come back.
about.changelog.line5: Packaged builds now include a SHA256 checksum file.
about.changelog.line6: English now covers the whole interface: settings, the Work Director, task records and message popups all follow the language you pick.
about.changelog.scratch: Temporary scripts and logs kept in the workspace's .ezness folder no longer ask for confirmation one by one, and error redirection no longer makes an ordinary command look unknown.
about.changelog.taskDrafts: The composer keeps a separate draft per conversation and task: switch away and back and your unsent text and picked files are still there, and never follow you into another task.

director.page.design.s1.body: Observe only flags things, it never assigns work. Suggest writes the split as a proposal for you to approve. Run dispatches directly. Workspaces outside its scope are never touched.
director.page.design.s1.title: 1. Check authority first
director.page.design.s10.body: When a project passes review and frees a slot, it looks for another project that's slow or waiting on review and sends the slot to help. If helping would mean two people writing the same files, it doesn't force it — it uses handoffs or review instead. If there's nothing worth helping with, the slot stays empty rather than dispatching work just to fill it.
director.page.design.s10.title: 10. Free slots help other projects
director.page.design.s11.body: Once every project is done and reviewed, it checks interfaces and seams against the review verdicts. If anything is unclear, it sends the related workers one more question-only task — answer, don't start building — then gives you the final call.
director.page.design.s11.title: 11. One last end-to-end check
director.page.design.s2.body1a: Every job gets a project file: the goal, the workspace, the tasks involved and the calls already made. Before starting it gives two estimates:
director.page.design.s2.body1e: . These aren't hard deadlines — they're its own checkpoints. When one passes it takes a look; if things are behind, it reassigns people.
director.page.design.s2.body2: It assigns one worker by default. Work is split only when the file sets don't overlap and each part can start on its own; small projects, single files and tightly coupled interfaces stay with one person. When one task depends on another (backend first, then frontend), the review waits for the earlier one to close out instead of judging half an interface.
director.page.design.s2.title: 2. Open a project file, give two times
director.page.design.s3.body: The dispatch limit is the number of desks. A worker holds one slot from build through review: when the build ends and a reviewer takes over, the slot passes to the reviewer, so headcount never exceeds your limit.
director.page.design.s3.title: 3. One task, one desk
director.page.design.s4.body1: The moment a worker stops, the director hands you that build: a file for a single-file job, the workspace path and entry point for a whole project, marked as a stage build. Only then does it schedule a reviewer — you don't have to wait for review to see something.
director.page.design.s4.body2b: a program that starts from its real entry point
director.page.design.s4.body2c: , not “the files are written”. Before handing over it checks itself: no stubs, mock servers, PYTHONPATH tricks or scratch scripts standing in for the real implementation, a launchable entry point, and a launch command with real output in the worker's reply. If that check fails, the handoff says so and the build isn't counted as done.
director.page.design.s4.title: 4. Build → hand to you → review
director.page.design.s5.body1: The reviewer is a separate task: it doesn't take a builder's seat and never edits source. It watches 3–6 key points: is the delivery a real implementation, are the files there, do the core features work, does the program start. It must actually launch the real entry point and put the command and the output it saw into the evidence; a file merely existing doesn't pass. It wraps up in 5–10 minutes with one of three verdicts: passed, failed, unverified.
director.page.design.s5.body2: No evidence means “unverified”, never passed. If the reviewer says passed but pre-checks find stubs or test artifacts, that doesn't pass either — it sends the work back once within the rework budget without involving you. Reviewers aren't reviewed themselves, so this can't recurse forever. When a task has a prerequisite, review starts after that delivery is closed out, not against half an interface.
director.page.design.s5.body3: Review is its job, not yours: if it can't reach a verdict it records “unverified” and says why, rather than handing you a “please check this”. If you want something re-checked, just say so.
director.page.design.s5.title: 5. Reviewers check, never edit
director.page.design.s6.body: When review fails, the original worker patches only the failed items and leaves what already passed alone. Rework is capped at 2 rounds by default (changeable in the settings above). Three things happen without asking: a failed review triggers rework, a delivery that looks like a test artifact is sent back, and a reviewer with no verdict records unverified. Only when the rework limit is reached and it still fails does it ask whether to try again.
director.page.design.s6.title: 6. Failures only patch the gaps
director.page.design.s7.body: One task done: a handoff message marked “in review”. Review has a verdict: it updates that same message instead of sending another. Whole project built but not yet reviewed: one “build complete, reviewing” message that later verdicts are added to. Rework, a stuck worker or a decision you need to make get their own alerts.
director.page.design.s7.title: 7. Reports follow the project, no spam
director.page.design.s8.body: The director listens in on each worker's status, output and tool calls to tell a model error from a dropped connection, a long silence or a loop. It tries in order: stop and restart, then switch model or task; only if none of that works does it report to you and say exactly where it's stuck.
director.page.design.s8.title: 8. Stuck workers get diagnosed first
director.page.design.s9.body: At any stage, if you tell it to stop, restart or change the task, it does. If you edit something inside a task and leave, it looks at what changed first: if your request is met it wraps up, otherwise it keeps assigning work.
director.page.design.s9.title: 9. Your words come first

settings.about.description: Ezness is a local-first desktop AI workbench. Chats, the work director, workspaces and tasks, file browsing, knowledge, the warehouse and prompts all live in one window. Connect a cloud API or run models locally with Ollama; web search, OCR and speech recognition turn on when needed, and idle features do not run in the background.
settings.about.env.desc: Version details help with troubleshooting; the usage below is counted locally and contains no keys, chat content or file text.
settings.about.env.title: Runtime and data
settings.about.features.agent.desc: Separate prompts, knowledge and memory; four permission levels; export and import agents and ability groups as a bundle.
settings.about.features.agent.title: Agents and AI abilities
settings.about.features.billing.desc: Common providers come with addresses filled in; pick one and add a key. You can also point at your own gateway.
settings.about.features.billing.title: Model providers and usage
settings.about.features.chat.desc: Switch models, attach files and stream answers you can stop at any time.
settings.about.features.chat.title: Chat
settings.about.features.desc: Features combine as you need them: the everyday ones stay on, the occasional ones open when used, and nothing dictates your workflow.
settings.about.features.director.desc: A standing director tracks progress, assigns work and reviews results; it reports only when something changes.
settings.about.features.director.title: Work director
settings.about.features.kb.desc: Local chunked retrieval with category and per-document scope; chat attachments are kept long-term in the warehouse.
settings.about.features.kb.title: Knowledge and warehouse
settings.about.features.prompts.desc: Templates live in your own data folder, ready to use and easy to add to.
settings.about.features.prompts.title: Prompt templates
settings.about.features.title: What it does
settings.about.features.web.desc: Searches leave from your machine, and OCR and speech recognition run locally — never through the model vendor.
settings.about.features.web.title: Web, OCR and voice
settings.about.features.workspace.desc: Local folders or remote SSH workspaces; expand the tree as needed, with text highlighting plus image preview and editing.
settings.about.features.workspace.title: Workspaces and files
settings.about.intro: Ezness is built independently by EasyBlue. Model connections, knowledge, workspaces and usage records stay on your own computer — no account, no cloud relay.
settings.about.note: Settings, chats, knowledge, the warehouse, prompt templates and usage records all live in the data folder below. The app has no cloud account and does not upload any of it; to move machines, copy the whole folder.
settings.about.principles.title: Design principles
settings.about.tagline: Take heavy tools apart and keep only the parts that help.
settings.about.title: About
settings.about.values.control.desc: Every provider, model, default and tool permission is in front of you; nothing behaves in a hidden way.
settings.about.values.control.title: Controlled
settings.about.values.light.desc: No component library, no resident background services — launching means launching.
settings.about.values.light.title: Lean
settings.about.values.local.desc: Settings, chats and files stay on your machine, and keys live only in the local config.
settings.about.values.local.title: Local-first
settings.about.values.transparent.desc: No accounts and no tracking; requests leave your machine only when you start them.
settings.about.values.transparent.title: Transparent
